build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: not picture 17: its packed bytes end on the disk where picture 44's packed bytes begin, and the unpacker reads on to the end of its 3-sector window, so these are those bytes decoded with picture 17's value table (side 1's, this snapshot's). Nothing reads them

comments.text: Picture 17's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($CA00, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it): the base frame at +$0049, channel 0's script at +$000E, channel 1's script at +$0027 and 0 for channels 2 and 3, which it does not use.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 8 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 5, frame 2 then 3, frame 2 then 7, frame 2 then 7, frame 2 then 3, frame 1 then 2, frame 3 then 12, frame 3 then 11. One pass takes 50 steps.

Channel 1's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 11 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 4 then 1, frame 5 then 1, frame 6 then 3, frame 6 then 1, frame 5 then 8, frame 5 then 1, frame 6 then 5, frame 6 then 10, frame 6 then 5, frame 6 then 1, frame 5 then 1. One pass takes 37 steps.

Picture 17's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $03 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 16 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 17, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 1 and 6: a run count of 0 to start, then 5 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 19 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 5 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 2 of picture 17, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 2, 3, 4 and 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 14 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 6 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 3 of picture 17, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 7 and 8: a run count of 0 to start, then 5 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 18 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 5 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
Frame 4 of picture 17, named by channel 1's entry 1: empty, a run count of 0 and the $FF that ends the frame, so draw_frame_xor ($0648) changes nothing and the entry only waits.

Frame 5 of picture 17, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 2, 5, 6 and 11: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 19 bitmap bytes in all (2 runs of a repeated byte among them), in columns 5 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 6 of picture 17, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 3, 4, 7, 8, 9 and 10: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 17 bitmap bytes in all (1 run of a repeated byte among them), in columns 6 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
The last byte picture 17's own packed bytes decode to, the 791st byte from $CA00: the unpacker makes it from the bits left over in the stream's last byte. Nothing reads it.
